Walt Disney did play a central role in creating Mickey Mouse, but the creation was collaborative [d2][d8]. According to Wikipedia and the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History, Mickey Mouse was co-created in 1928 by Walt Disney and animator Ub Iwerks [d2][d8]. Disney conceived the idea for the character — reportedly on a train ride home from New York after losing the rights to his earlier character Oswald the Lucky Rabbit — while Iwerks was the one who physically designed and drew Mickey Mouse [d1][d7]. As NPR notes, Disney was integral to Mickey's success, defining the character's personality and voicing him for years, but it was Iwerks who designed the iconic cartoon [d3]. Britannica and CNN broadly attribute Mickey's creation to Disney [d4][d5], while more detailed accounts from the Walt Disney Family Museum, Wikipedia, and the Smithsonian clarify that Iwerks was an essential co-creator [d1][d2][d8]. In short, Walt Disney was a co-creator of Mickey Mouse, contributing the concept and character direction, while Ub Iwerks provided the visual design and animation [d2][d3][d8].
